title: EmoRAG: Evaluating RAG Robustness to Symbolic Perturbations

problem.claim: RAG systems need robustness to symbolic perturbations that can alter retrieval and generated output.

gap.claim: The susceptibility of RAG systems to subtle symbolic perturbations, including near-imperceptible emoticons, has been overlooked.

contributions.claim: The study characterizes EmoRAG, in which injecting a single emoticon into a query can cause retrieval of semantically unrelated texts containing a matching emoticon.
The study analyzes single-emoticon disruption, positional sensitivity, and vulnerability associated with larger model parameter scales across question-answering and code domains.
The study evaluates standard defenses and proposes targeted defenses for emoticon-based perturbations, including analysis of their strengths and limitations.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that a single emoticon injection makes retrieval of semantically unrelated texts nearly 100% likely when those texts contain a matching emoticon.

Across general question-answering and code domains using multiple state-of-the-art retrievers and generators, the authors report that a single emoticon can almost completely dominate RAG output, beginning-position emoticons produce F1-Scores exceeding 0.92 across datasets, and larger models are more vulnerable.
The authors report that standard defenses are insufficient and that targeted defenses have strengths and limitations against emoticon-based perturbations.

narrative_sequence.summary: RAG systems use external knowledge to improve LLM faithfulness.
The study identifies severe susceptibility to subtle symbolic perturbations, especially emoticons.
Experiments report strong disruption, positional sensitivity, and greater vulnerability in larger models.
The study analyzes underlying mechanisms and frames the vulnerability as a possible adversarial manipulation threat.
The study evaluates standard defenses, proposes targeted defenses, and outlines future directions for robust RAG systems.

source_observation.claim: A single symbolic token can dominate retrieval and substantially disrupt RAG output.

interpretation.claim: RAG robustness evaluation should test minimal, semantically irrelevant symbolic perturbations rather than only conventional textual noise.

application.claim: Add single-symbol and position-controlled perturbation tests to RAG retrieval and generation evaluations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the reported vulnerability generalizes beyond emoticons, the named domains, or the evaluated systems.

source_observation.claim: Standard defenses were reported as insufficient against the perturbation.

interpretation.claim: Robustness mitigation should be assessed against the specific perturbation mechanism rather than assumed from general defenses.

application.claim: Benchmark targeted defenses together with their strengths and limitations under emoticon-based attacks.

exception.claim: The abstract does not identify the defenses evaluated or quantify their mitigation performance.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, retrievers, generators, baselines, or experimental configurations.
The underlying mechanisms are not described.
The targeted defenses and their quantitative results are not described.
The threat model and adversary capabilities are not specified.
Independent verification, reproducibility, and full-text findings are unavailable.
